Subject: SLA exposure & chargeback visualization — design + data ask

Hi team,

Quick ask from my side — ACME (Lisa + procurement) raised a follow-up from last week's licensing conversation: they want two things visible in the Console during their renewal review:

1) SLA exposure heatmap: a per-route view showing % of requests off-SLO over rolling 7/30 day windows, with the ability to filter by region and model family.
2) Chargeback alignment: a visualization that maps token/route spend to customer-defined billing buckets so we can show "what drove the overage" in plain terms.

They're asking for a demo on Tues so we need a tight proposal for what the Console can show (mockups + the minimum telemetry / aggregation we need).

Can you help outline:
- Laura: UX options — quick wireframes or screenshots we can demo (no polished polish)
- Markus: data model + query cost — what rollups do we need from streaming telemetry, and rough estimate of storage/compute impact for 7/30d windows?
- Marissa: any legal/CS talking points about what we can expose re: tenant-level SLA metrics (privacy/contract constraints)?

I've attached a rough PoC screenshot + a short spec. If we can sync for 30 minutes today or tomorrow AM that'd be ideal.

Thanks,

--
Jordan Blake
Director, Growth & GTM
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — great prompt.

High-level UX ideas below (I put very rough thumbnails in the attached PNG):

Option A — "Exposure lanes": a horizontal timeline per route with color intensity for %off-SLO. Hover reveals counts (tokens, requests, %off). Pros: compact, good for comparing many routes.

Option B — "Stacked breakdown": stacked bar per day showing token spend by billing bucket and overlaid SLO breaches (red stripes). Pros: ties spend + breaches in one view.

Option C — "Top-k causes" panel: along the right, list routes that contributed >5% of SLA breaches or >10% of chargeback variance in the window. Click-to-drill to tenant examples.

Questions for data: can we get per-route daily rollups for these dimensions? if not, we'll need a sampling/aggregation plan.

Happy to sketch a 5-slide demo deck this afternoon.

-Laura

Jordan/Laura — quick technical readout.

Summary of what we need and feasibility:
- Telemetry required: per-request route id, tenant id, timestamp, model variant, latency_ms, token_count, outcome (success/err), and whether fallback occurred.
- Aggregation: we can maintain daily and hourly rollups keyed by {route, region, tenant, model_family} with counters: total_requests, total_tokens, total_breaches (latency > configured SLO), fallback_count.
- SLA exposure metric = total_breaches / total_requests (windowed). Chargeback mapping requires attribution labels on routes (billing_bucket) — either stored on route config or a join table.

Performance/cost back-of-envelope:
- For prod fleet (~1.2B requests/day), computing hourly rollups across route × region × model_family would add ~4-6% to our ingestion pipeline CPU and ~10% to Kafka storage for 30-day retention unless we compress.
- If we limit to top 5k routes by traffic (Pareto), cost drops ~70% and still covers ~92% of spend.

Attachments: I included a sample mapping doc (chargeback-mapping-spec.docx).

Next steps I recommend:
1) agree on minimal key dimensions (route, region, billing_bucket)
2) implement hourly rollup consumer + a small OLAP table for the Console queries
3) provide a product-facing API that returns top causes + drilldowns.

I can scope an initial spike for 2 sprints.

-Markus

Quick compliance note: exposing tenant-level SLA breach rates is fine from a privacy perspective (no PII), but we need to ensure contract language allows per-tenant performance summaries — some enterprise customers have explicit clause about "no public disclosure of performance vs peers". For ACME specifically, procurement said they're ok with a tenant-only view (they won't show peer comparisons) — still, we should include a small disclaimer and an audit log of who viewed the data.

Also: if we allow drill-to-tenant examples (trace links), ensure access is constrained to users with tenant access and that we redacted request payload previews. I'll sync with security on audit events for "Console > SLA view".

-Marissa
